intent.raw_query: Safari Kenya family of 3, $8000, 10 days, July 2026

experiences.name: Maasai Mara Great Migration Safari
experiences.description: Witness the world-famous Great Migration where millions of wildebeest, zebras, and gazelles cross the Mara River. Game drives in open 4x4 vehicles offer close encounters with the Big Five and dramatic predator-prey interactions in one of Africa's most iconic wildlife spectacles.
experiences.location: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County

experiences.name: Amboseli Elephant Watching with Kilimanjaro Views
experiences.description: Observe massive elephant herds roaming the savannah with the snow-capped peak of Mount Kilimanjaro as a dramatic backdrop. Amboseli is home to some of Africa's largest tuskers and offers exceptional photography opportunities at sunrise when the mountain is clearest.

experiences.name: Lake Nakuru Flamingo and Rhino Safari
experiences.description: Explore the alkaline shores of Lake Nakuru, famously painted pink by thousands of flamingos. The national park is also a critical sanctuary for both black and white rhinos, as well as leopards, lions, and Rothschild giraffes, making it one of Kenya's most diverse wildlife destinations.
experiences.location: Lake Nakuru National Park, Nakuru County

experiences.name: Ol Pejeta Conservancy Chimpanzee Sanctuary Visit
experiences.description: Visit East Africa's largest chimpanzee sanctuary at Ol Pejeta Conservancy, home to rescued chimps from across Africa. The conservancy also protects the last two northern white rhinos on Earth and offers guided bush walks and night game drives for a truly immersive wildlife experience.

experiences.name: Tsavo East Red Elephant Game Drive
experiences.description: Discover the vast red-dusted plains of Tsavo East, Kenya's largest national park, where elephants stained red by volcanic soil roam freely. Spot lions, cheetahs, hippos at Aruba Dam, and massive herds of buffalo across dramatic landscapes with far fewer crowds than other reserves.
experiences.location: Tsavo East National Park, Taita-Taveta County

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Kenya
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled - in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and arrange pre-booked budget airport shuttle or shared matatu transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in and settle into your beachfront accommodation.

meals.breakfast: Meal on flight or skip
meals.lunch: Meal on flight or airport snack
meals.dinner: Grab a quick affordable bite at the airport arrivals hall (budget kiosks available, ~KES 500-800) or pack snacks for late arrival

day_by_day.notes: Arrival day only. Pre-book your airport transfer in advance to save money — shared shuttles cost significantly less than private taxis. Keep KES 2,000-3,000 in cash handy for tips and small expenses on arrival night. Confirm hotel check-in arrangements for late arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery after late arrival. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort. Take a relaxed orientation walk along the beachfront to get familiar with the local area, nearby shops, and transport options. Explore the immediate coastal surroundings and enjoy the warm 25°C weather.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the local market near the resort to pick up snacks, water, and supplies for upcoming days. Explore the nearby coastal village on foot — browse local craft stalls, interact with vendors, and get a feel for Kenyan coastal culture. Look for budget souvenir items like kikoi fabrics and beaded jewelry.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset stroll along the beach. Enjoy dinner at a local 'mama mboga' style restaurant or a budget beach-side eatery serving fresh Swahili coastal cuisine. Try nyama choma (grilled meat) or grilled fish with ugali.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast or local tea shop with mandazi and chai (~KES 200-300)
meals.lunch: Fresh fruit from local market stalls and a light snack (~KES 300-400)
meals.dinner: Local beachside restaurant serving grilled fish, ugali, and sukuma wiki (~KES 600-900)

day_by_day.notes: Use this day to recover from jet lag. Exchange currency at a local forex bureau rather than the airport for better rates. Download the M-Pesa app if possible — it is widely used for payments across Kenya and can save on transaction fees.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning birdwatching walk along the coastal forest or mangrove area near the resort. Kenya's coast is rich with hornbills, sunbirds, and kingfishers. Bring binoculars if available. This is a free or very low-cost activity perfect for wildlife and nature lovers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a budget matatu or tuk-tuk ride to explore a nearby nature reserve or marine park. Snorkel in the shallow reef waters to observe colorful fish and coral — rent basic snorkel gear locally (~KES 500-700). The warm July waters make this ideal for marine wildlife viewing.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area. Visit a local food market for a self-catered dinner option — buy fresh chapati, beans, and vegetables to keep costs low. Alternatively, dine at a budget local eatery.

meals.breakfast: Chai and mandazi at a local tea house (~KES 150-250)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from local market — samosas, roasted corn, fresh coconut water (~KES 300-500)
meals.dinner: Budget local restaurant: beans, rice, and kachumbari salad (~KES 500-700)

day_by_day.notes: July is dry season on the Kenyan coast with only ~30mm of rain expected — perfect for snorkeling and outdoor activities. Apply high SPF sunscreen as UV levels are strong. Carry at least 1.5 liters of water when out exploring.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day budget safari excursion — book a shared group safari to a nearby national park or reserve (e.g., Shimba Hills National Reserve if on the south coast, or Arabuko-Sokoke Forest Reserve). Depart early morning around 06:00-07:00 for the best wildlife viewing. Look for elephants, buffalo, leopards, and colobus monkeys.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the safari game drive through the reserve. Enjoy a packed picnic lunch at a designated park picnic site to save on costs. Watch for giraffes, zebras, warthogs, and abundant birdlife in the warm afternoon light.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by late afternoon. Rest and freshen up. Enjoy a casual dinner at the resort or a nearby local eatery. Share safari stories with fellow travelers.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at resort or packed from local bakery (~KES 200-400)
meals.lunch: Packed picnic lunch prepared from market supplies the evening before (~KES 400-600)
meals.dinner: Local restaurant near resort: pilau rice with chicken or goat stew (~KES 700-1,000)

day_by_day.notes: Book shared group safari vehicles in advance through local budget tour operators — shared costs can bring the price down to KES 3,000-5,000 per person including park fees. Wear neutral-colored clothing (khaki, olive, beige) for wildlife viewing. Bring a jacket for early morning game drives as it can be cool.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a local nature conservancy or community-run wildlife sanctuary near the resort. Many coastal Kenya communities run affordable conservation projects where visitors can learn about local wildlife, tree planting initiatives, and turtle conservation programs. Entry fees are minimal and support local communities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a nearby historical site or coastal fort (such as Fort Jesus in Mombasa if accessible) to understand Kenya's Swahili and colonial history. Walk through the old town area to admire traditional carved doors, mosques, and colorful architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the local night food market. Try street food classics: mutura (Kenyan sausage), roasted maize, and fresh juice. This is an authentic, budget-friendly Kenyan evening experience.

meals.breakfast: Local tea room: chai, eggs, and toast (~KES 250-400)
meals.lunch: Street food near historical site: samosas, bhajias, and fresh mango juice (~KES 400-600)
meals.dinner: Night market street food: mutura, roasted maize, and mandazi (~KES 400-600)

day_by_day.notes: Community conservancies typically charge KES 500-1,500 entry. Fort Jesus UNESCO entry is ~KES 1,200 for non-residents — worth the investment for history enthusiasts. Keep valuables secure in crowded market areas.

day_by_day.morning: Second safari day — arrange a budget shared safari to a different reserve or a morning game drive extension. Focus on birdwatching this morning as Kenya's coast hosts over 300 bird species. Hire a local birding guide for a few hours (~KES 1,000-1,500) for an enriching and affordable experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return by midday. Spend the afternoon at the beach — swimming, relaxing, and enjoying the natural coastal environment. Collect shells, observe shore birds, and enjoy the warm July sunshine. This is a completely free afternoon activity.
day_by_day.evening: Cook or arrange a self-catered dinner using fresh seafood purchased directly from local fishermen on the beach — often much cheaper than restaurants. Alternatively, visit a budget beach restaurant for fresh grilled prawns or fish.

meals.breakfast: Resort or local café: fruit salad, bread, and chai (~KES 300-500)
meals.lunch: Beach snacks: fresh coconut, roasted cashews, and tropical fruit (~KES 300-400)
meals.dinner: Fresh grilled fish or prawns bought from local fishermen and grilled at a budget beach shack (~KES 800-1,200)

day_by_day.notes: Negotiate directly with local fishermen for the freshest and most affordable seafood. Early morning (around 06:00-07:00) is the best time to buy fresh catch straight off the boats. Stay hydrated throughout the day.

day_by_day.morning: Take a budget dhow boat trip along the coastline. Traditional wooden dhow rides are an iconic Kenyan coastal experience and can be arranged affordably through local boat operators (~KES 1,500-2,500 for a shared trip). Look for dolphins, sea turtles, and diverse seabirds along the way.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at a sandbank or small island for a swim and snorkel session. Explore the underwater marine life — coral gardens, tropical fish, and starfish. Bring your own snacks and water to avoid overpriced on-boat refreshments.
day_by_day.evening: Return from dhow trip by late afternoon. Sunset walk along the beach. Dinner at a local Swahili restaurant — try biryani, coconut fish curry, or pilipili prawns for an authentic coastal Kenyan meal.

meals.breakfast: Mandazi and chai at local tea house (~KES 200-300)
meals.lunch: Packed snacks on the dhow: bread, fruit, and water (~KES 300-500)
meals.dinner: Swahili restaurant: coconut fish curry with rice and kachumbari (~KES 700-1,000)

day_by_day.notes: Negotiate dhow trip prices in advance and confirm what is included. Group bookings of 4-6 people significantly reduce per-person costs. Apply reef-safe sunscreen to protect the marine ecosystem. Bring a dry bag for electronics on the dhow.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to a nearby national park for a final major safari experience — consider Tsavo East or Tsavo West National Park if accessible via budget shared transport. These are among Africa's largest national parks and are known for red elephants, lions, cheetahs, and dramatic landscapes. Depart very early (05:30-06:00) for maximum wildlife activity.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue game drive in the park. Visit a natural landmark such as Mzima Springs (Tsavo West) where hippos and crocodiles can be observed from an underwater viewing chamber — a truly unique wildlife experience. Enjoy a packed picnic lunch at a park rest area.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort by evening. Celebrate the penultimate safari day with a slightly upgraded dinner at a mid-range local restaurant as a treat — still budget-conscious but a step up from street food.

meals.breakfast: Very early light breakfast: packed bread, banana, and thermos chai (~KES 200-300)
meals.lunch: Packed picnic at Tsavo park rest area (~KES 500-700)
meals.dinner: Local restaurant treat: nyama choma platter with kachumbari and ugali (~KES 1,000-1,500)

day_by_day.notes: Tsavo National Park entry fees apply (~KES 3,000-5,000 per person for non-residents). Book shared safari vehicles well in advance. This is a long day — expect 10-12 hours of travel and game driving. Wear comfortable, breathable clothing and bring a hat and sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed morning at the resort. Pack souvenirs and gifts. Take a final morning walk along the beach to appreciate the coastal scenery. Visit a local craft cooperative to purchase authentic Kenyan souvenirs — kikoi wraps, Maasai beaded jewelry, wooden carvings, and batik fabrics at fair prices.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local botanical garden or nature trail for a final nature experience. Many coastal areas have free or low-cost walking trails through indigenous coastal forest where you can spot chameleons, butterflies, and exotic plants. Alternatively, take a guided mangrove kayak tour (~KES 1,500-2,000).
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at your favorite local restaurant discovered during the trip. Reflect on the safari experiences, wildlife encounters, and cultural discoveries. Try a Kenyan dessert like mandazi with honey or fresh tropical fruit platter.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast as a final treat or local café (~KES 400-600)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a local eatery: chapati and lentil stew (~KES 500-700)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at best local restaurant from the trip: grilled fish, pilau, and fresh juice (~KES 800-1,200)

day_by_day.notes: Bargaining is expected at craft markets but always remain respectful. Aim for a fair price rather than the lowest possible — supporting local artisans is important. Pack souvenirs carefully to avoid damage. Confirm departure logistics and transport to the airport for the next day.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Kenya. Wake up early for one last sunrise beach walk — a peaceful and memorable way to end the trip. Enjoy a final Kenyan breakfast. Complete packing and check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Arrange budget shared shuttle or matatu transfer to the airport.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart for the airport with ample time for check-in and security. Browse airport duty-free for any final Kenyan coffee, tea, or small gifts. Reflect on 10 incredible days of safari, wildlife, and coastal nature in Kenya.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Kenya. Carry memories of wildlife encounters, Swahili coastal culture, and the stunning natural beauty of East Africa.

meals.breakfast: Final Kenyan breakfast: chai, eggs, toast, and fresh tropical fruit (~KES 400-600)
meals.lunch: Airport café or packed snacks for the journey (~KES 600-1,000)
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport restaurant depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for airport check-in and security. Keep some KES for final transport and tips. Declare any wildlife products (shells, feathers, plants) at customs — many are restricted. Ensure all receipts for souvenirs are retained as proof of legal purchase. Safe travels!

trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled - in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport at 22:30. Clear immigration and customs, collect luggage, and meet your pre-arranged transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get settled into your beachfront accommodation.

meals.breakfast: On the flight
meals.lunch: On the flight or at the airport
meals.dinner: Light late-night snack or room service at Aegean Bliss Resort upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange airport transfer in advance to avoid delays at night. Keep essentials in carry-on for easy access. The resort's 24-hour front desk will accommodate your late check-in. Exchange some currency to Kenyan Shillings (KES) at the airport for small expenses.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a leisurely late start to recover from travel. After a relaxed breakfast at the resort, take a gentle orientation walk along the beachfront and explore the resort grounds. Familiarize yourself with the local area and visit a nearby local market to pick up supplies and soak in the coastal Kenyan atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to a nearby nature reserve or coastal forest walk for a gentle introduction to Kenya's natural environment. Spot coastal birdlife, butterflies, and tropical vegetation. Visit a local cultural center to learn about Kenyan coastal Swahili culture and history.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset stroll along the beach at Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy the warm July evening on the beachfront terrace, watching the Indian Ocean sunset before a relaxed dinner at the resort.

meals.breakfast: Full buffet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — enjoy fresh tropical fruits, eggs, and local Kenyan chai tea
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a nearby local coastal eatery — try grilled fish, coconut rice, and kachumbari (fresh tomato-onion salad) for around KES 800–1,200
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort's beachfront restaurant — fresh seafood platter with ugali or rice, budget approximately KES 2,000–3,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Day 2 is intentionally relaxed to allow recovery from long-haul travel and jet lag. Drink plenty of water as the warm 25°C July weather can be dehydrating. Apply sunscreen even on cloudy days. Confirm all upcoming safari bookings with the resort concierge today.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early by road or domestic flight to Tsavo East National Park for the Tsavo East Red Elephant Game Drive. Arrive in time for a morning game drive across the iconic red-dusted plains. Spot the famous red elephants coated in Tsavo's distinctive rust-colored soil, along with lions, buffalo, and giraffes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the afternoon game drive deeper into Tsavo East, exploring the Galana River corridor where crocodiles and hippos congregate. Visit Lugard Falls, a stunning series of rapids carved through ancient volcanic rock. Enjoy a packed bush picnic lunch in a scenic spot within the park.
day_by_day.evening: Return to your mid-range tented camp or lodge within or near Tsavo East for check-in. Freshen up and enjoy sundowner drinks as the African sun sets over the vast savannah plains. Attend a brief wildlife briefing by the camp naturalist.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort before departure — grab-and-go option with sandwiches and fruit
meals.lunch: Packed bush picnic lunch arranged by the game drive operator — sandwiches, fruit, juice, and local snacks
meals.dinner: Dinner at the Tsavo East lodge/camp — three-course set menu featuring Kenyan-style stew, grilled meats, and fresh vegetables, approximately KES 3,000–4,500 per person

day_by_day.notes: Wear neutral-colored clothing (khaki, olive, beige) for game drives — avoid bright colors that disturb wildlife. Bring binoculars, a camera with a zoom lens, and insect repellent. July is dry season in Tsavo, making wildlife sightings excellent as animals gather around water sources. Confirm transfer logistics the evening before.

day_by_day.morning: Rise before dawn for an early morning game drive in Tsavo East — the golden hour is the best time to spot predators returning from night hunts. Look for leopards in acacia trees, cheetahs on open plains, and large elephant herds moving to watering holes. The cool morning air makes this the most comfortable drive of the day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Mudanda Rock viewpoint, a massive inselberg that acts as a natural water catchment, attracting hundreds of elephants and other wildlife. Spend time at the viewing platform observing the incredible congregation of animals. Head back to camp for a midday rest during the hottest part of the day.
day_by_day.evening: Optional guided bush walk with an armed ranger around the lodge perimeter at dusk — a thrilling way to experience the African bush on foot and spot smaller wildlife, tracks, and insects. Return for a campfire dinner under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at camp before the dawn drive — tea, coffee, toast, and boiled eggs
meals.lunch: Lunch at the lodge — buffet-style with salads, grilled chicken, rice, and fresh fruit, approximately KES 1,500–2,500
meals.dinner: Campfire barbecue dinner at the lodge — nyama choma (grilled meat), roasted vegetables, and traditional Kenyan sides, approximately KES 2,500–4,000

day_by_day.notes: Tsavo East receives only 30mm of rain in July, so dust can be significant on game drives — bring a buff or light scarf to cover your face. Stay hydrated throughout the day. Tipping your game drive guide KES 500–1,000 per day is customary and greatly appreciated.

day_by_day.morning: Check out from Tsavo East and transfer to Amboseli National Park (approximately 3–4 hours by road through scenic Kenyan countryside). Arrive in time for a late morning game drive to witness the iconic sight of massive elephant herds roaming the savannah with the snow-capped peak of Mount Kilimanjaro as a dramatic backdrop.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Amboseli Elephant Watching experience, venturing to the Observation Hill viewpoint for a panoramic 360-degree view of the entire park. Spot buffalo, wildebeest, zebras, and hundreds of elephants gathering at the park's swamps. The clear July skies offer exceptional Kilimanjaro views in the afternoon light.
day_by_day.evening: Check in to a mid-range Amboseli lodge or tented camp. Enjoy the magical experience of watching elephants silhouetted against the golden Kilimanjaro backdrop at sunset — one of Kenya's most iconic wildlife photography moments.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Tsavo East lodge before checkout
meals.lunch: Stop at a roadside local restaurant en route to Amboseli — try a hearty plate of githeri (maize and bean stew) or pilau rice for KES 400–800
meals.dinner: Dinner at Amboseli lodge — buffet featuring East African cuisine with fresh vegetables, grilled meats, and local desserts, approximately KES 3,000–4,500

day_by_day.notes: The transfer between Tsavo East and Amboseli passes through Kimana — a good stop for fuel and refreshments. Amboseli is renowned for having the best Kilimanjaro views in the morning before clouds build, so plan your drives accordingly. The park is also excellent for birdwatching with over 400 species recorded.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn wake-up for the ultimate Amboseli experience — a sunrise game drive with Kilimanjaro glowing pink and orange in the morning light. This is the clearest time of day for mountain views. Focus on the elephant families emerging from the swamps, and look for lions and hyenas from overnight hunts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local Maasai village (manyatta) near Amboseli for an authentic cultural experience. Learn about traditional Maasai warrior culture, see traditional homesteads, watch jumping dances, and purchase handcrafted beaded jewelry directly from artisans. This interaction supports local community livelihoods.
day_by_day.evening: Final sunset game drive in Amboseli, specifically targeting the famous Amboseli elephant matriarchs and their families at the swamps. Return to camp for a relaxed evening with fellow travelers, sharing wildlife stories around the campfire.

meals.breakfast: Light pre-dawn snack before the drive — tea, coffee, and biscuits provided by the camp; full breakfast upon return
meals.lunch: Lunch at the lodge — light salads, sandwiches, and fresh juice, approximately KES 1,500–2,000
meals.dinner: Special Maasai-inspired dinner at the lodge featuring traditional recipes — sukuma wiki, ugali, and roasted goat, approximately KES 2,500–3,500

day_by_day.notes: When visiting the Maasai village, negotiate the entrance fee (typically KES 1,000–2,000 per person) beforehand. Photography of Maasai people requires permission and may involve a small fee. Bring small denomination KES notes for purchasing crafts. Respect local customs and dress modestly during the visit.

day_by_day.morning: Check out from Amboseli and transfer to Nairobi (approximately 4 hours), then connect by road or domestic flight to the Maasai Mara. Arrive at the Mara in the afternoon. If time permits, check in to your mid-range Mara camp and take a brief orientation drive to get your bearings in this world-famous ecosystem.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin the Maasai Mara Great Migration Safari experience with an afternoon game drive along the Mara River — the most dramatic crossing point where wildebeest brave crocodile-infested waters. July is peak migration season, offering the best chance of witnessing a river crossing, one of nature's greatest spectacles.
day_by_day.evening: Return to camp as the sun sets over the golden Mara plains. Enjoy sundowner drinks at a scenic viewpoint overlooking the endless grasslands. Attend a camp briefing about tomorrow's full-day migration safari strategy.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Amboseli lodge before checkout
meals.lunch: Packed lunch in the vehicle during the transfer or at a roadside restaurant near Narok — try a local Kenyan lunch for KES 600–1,000
meals.dinner: Welcome dinner at the Mara camp — three-course meal with soup, main course of Kenyan game or chicken stew, and dessert, approximately KES 3,500–5,000

day_by_day.notes: The Nairobi to Maasai Mara road transfer passes through Narok town — a good stop for supplies. Alternatively, a 45-minute domestic flight from Wilson Airport in Nairobi to one of the Mara airstrips is a worthwhile splurge for a mid-range budget. July is peak season in the Mara, so ensure accommodation is pre-booked well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day immersion in the Maasai Mara Great Migration Safari. Depart at dawn for prime positioning along the Mara River crossing points. Witness the extraordinary spectacle of thousands of wildebeest and zebras nervously gathering on the riverbank before plunging into the crocodile-filled waters. The sounds, dust, and raw energy of this event are unforgettable.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the migration safari across the open Mara plains, following vast herds of wildebeest stretching to the horizon. Spot the predators that follow the migration — lions, cheetahs, leopards, and spotted hyenas. Visit the Mara Triangle for excellent big cat sightings in the well-managed western section of the reserve.
day_by_day.evening: Optional hot air balloon safari at dawn the following morning can be booked today (approximately USD 450–500 per person — a worthwhile splurge). This evening, enjoy a bush dinner set up in the open savannah under a canopy of stars — a magical mid-range camp experience.

meals.breakfast: Pre-dawn bush breakfast in the vehicle — thermos of tea/coffee, sandwiches, and fruit provided by the camp
meals.lunch: Bush picnic lunch at a scenic Mara River viewpoint — packed by the camp with sandwiches, salads, and cold drinks
meals.dinner: Special open-air bush dinner in the savannah — candlelit tables, three-course meal, and the sounds of the African night, approximately KES 4,000–6,000

day_by_day.notes: River crossings are unpredictable — patience is essential. Your guide will monitor radio communications with other guides to identify the best crossing locations. Bring a rain jacket as July afternoons can occasionally bring light showers (30mm monthly average). Keep noise to a minimum near crossing points to avoid disturbing the herds.

day_by_day.morning: Transfer north to Lake Nakuru National Park (approximately 4–5 hours from the Mara via the scenic Rift Valley escarpment). En route, stop at the dramatic Rift Valley viewpoint for panoramic photographs of the Great Rift Valley — one of Africa's most spectacular geological features. Arrive at Lake Nakuru for a late morning game drive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin the Lake Nakuru Flamingo and Rhino Safari in earnest. The alkaline lake shores turn pink with thousands of lesser and greater flamingos feeding in the shallows. Search for both black and white rhinos — Lake Nakuru is one of Kenya's best rhino sanctuaries. Also spot lions, leopards, Rothschild giraffes, and waterbuck.
day_by_day.evening: Check in to a mid-range lodge near Lake Nakuru. Enjoy the stunning views over the lake as the flamingo flocks create a spectacular pink haze in the evening light. Relax with a sundowner on the lodge terrace.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the Mara camp before departure
meals.lunch: Stop in Naivasha town for lunch at a local restaurant — try tilapia fish from Lake Naivasha with ugali and sukuma wiki for KES 800–1,200
meals.dinner: Dinner at the Lake Nakuru lodge — buffet with a variety of Kenyan and international dishes, approximately KES 2,500–4,000

day_by_day.notes: The Rift Valley viewpoint stop near Mai Mahiu is approximately 1 hour from Nairobi — a perfect photo opportunity. Lake Nakuru National Park is fully fenced, making it excellent for rhino and lion sightings. The flamingo numbers vary seasonally depending on water levels and algae growth. July typically offers good flamingo concentrations.

day_by_day.morning: Final early morning game drive in Lake Nakuru National Park, specifically targeting rhino sightings in the early hours when they are most active. Visit Baboon Cliff viewpoint for a sweeping panorama of the entire lake and its flamingo-pink shoreline — the perfect final wildlife memory of Kenya.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Ol Pejeta Conservancy Chimpanzee Sanctuary (approximately 3 hours from Lake Nakuru via Nyahururu). Meet East Africa's rescued chimpanzees in their spacious sanctuary enclosures and learn about the conservation work protecting these endangered primates. Ol Pejeta is also home to the last two northern white rhinos on Earth.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to Nairobi (approximately 3.5 hours from Ol Pejeta) for final shopping at the Maasai Market or Utamaduni Craft Centre for authentic Kenyan souvenirs. Enjoy a farewell dinner in Nairobi before your onward journey or overnight at a Nairobi airport hotel if departing the next day.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Lake Nakuru lodge before the final game drive
meals.lunch: Lunch at Ol Pejeta Conservancy's visitor center café — light meals, sandwiches, and cold drinks, approximately KES 1,000–1,800
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a Nairobi restaurant — treat yourself to a mid-range Kenyan steakhouse like Carnivore Restaurant or a rooftop restaurant in Westlands, approximately KES 3,000–5,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Ol Pejeta Conservancy charges a separate conservation fee (approximately USD 90 per person per day) which supports critical wildlife conservation work including protecting the last northern white rhinos. Budget for this entry fee. If departing Kenya tonight, ensure you allow at least 3 hours before your flight for the Nairobi transfer and airport procedures. Purchase a quality Kenyan coffee blend as a souvenir — Kenya produces some of the world's finest arabica coffee.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Kenya Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Maasai Mara Great Migration Safari
experiences.description: Witness the world-famous Great Migration where millions of wildebeest, zebras, and gazelles cross the Mara River. Game drives in open 4x4 vehicles offer close encounters with the Big Five and dramatic predator-prey interactions in one of Africa's most iconic wildlife spectacles.
experiences.location: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County

experiences.name: Amboseli Elephant Watching with Kilimanjaro Views
experiences.description: Observe massive elephant herds roaming the savannah with the snow-capped peak of Mount Kilimanjaro as a dramatic backdrop. Amboseli is home to some of Africa's largest tuskers and offers exceptional photography opportunities at sunrise when the mountain is clearest.

experiences.name: Lake Nakuru Flamingo and Rhino Safari
experiences.description: Explore the alkaline shores of Lake Nakuru, famously painted pink by thousands of flamingos. The national park is also a critical sanctuary for both black and white rhinos, as well as leopards, lions, and Rothschild giraffes, making it one of Kenya's most diverse wildlife destinations.
experiences.location: Lake Nakuru National Park, Nakuru County

experiences.name: Ol Pejeta Conservancy Chimpanzee Sanctuary Visit
experiences.description: Visit East Africa's largest chimpanzee sanctuary at Ol Pejeta Conservancy, home to rescued chimps from across Africa. The conservancy also protects the last two northern white rhinos on Earth and offers guided bush walks and night game drives for a truly immersive wildlife experience.

experiences.name: Tsavo East Red Elephant Game Drive
experiences.description: Discover the vast red-dusted plains of Tsavo East, Kenya's largest national park, where elephants stained red by volcanic soil roam freely. Spot lions, cheetahs, hippos at Aruba Dam, and massive herds of buffalo across dramatic landscapes with far fewer crowds than other reserves.
experiences.location: Tsavo East National Park, Taita-Taveta County

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight UA arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrival at Nairobi/Mombasa airport at 22:30. Private luxury transfer arranged to Aegean Bliss Resort. Welcome drink and late-night light supper upon check-in. Resort orientation briefing with personal concierge.

meals.breakfast: On board flight
meals.lunch: On board flight
meals.dinner: Late-night welcome supper at Aegean Bliss Resort — curated charcuterie board, fresh tropical fruits, and Kenyan herbal teas served in-suite or at the private lounge

day_by_day.notes: Ensure private airport transfer is pre-booked through the resort. Pack a light layer for the evening coastal breeze. No strenuous activities on Day 1 — rest and acclimatization are the priority.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely resort morning — enjoy a gourmet breakfast on your private beachfront terrace. Take a guided orientation walk of the resort grounds, including the private beach, infinity pool, and lush coastal gardens. Snorkeling session in the warm Indian Ocean waters just off the resort's private beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Embark on a guided coastal nature walk through nearby mangrove forests with a resident naturalist. Learn about Kenya's coastal ecosystems, bird species, and marine conservation efforts. Return to the resort for a private spa session — choose from a Swahili-inspired massage or a Baobab oil treatment.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the beach with a private butler. Enjoy a curated Swahili fusion dinner at the resort's signature oceanfront restaurant under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at the resort's beachfront terrace — fresh tropical fruits, Kenyan coffee, eggs Benedict, smoked fish platters
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch — grilled lobster, coconut prawn salad, and fresh mango smoothies at the resort's Aqua Lounge
meals.dinner: Swahili fusion tasting menu at the resort's signature restaurant — featuring dishes like coconut-braised Mombasa crab, pilau rice, and tamarind-glazed snapper with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Day 2 is designed for gentle recovery after the long-haul flight. UV index is high — apply reef-safe sunscreen. The warm July weather (avg 25°C) is perfect for outdoor coastal activities.

day_by_day.morning: Private sunrise game drive in Tsavo East National Park — Embark on the Tsavo East Red Elephant Game Drive. Depart early at 06:00 in a luxury 4x4 Land Cruiser with a professional guide. Witness the iconic red-dusted elephants roaming the vast Tsavo plains at golden hour. Look out for lions, buffalos, and giraffes in the early morning light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Tsavo East game drive through the Galana River area, a prime wildlife corridor. Enjoy a gourmet bush picnic lunch set up by your guide in a scenic spot. Afternoon game drive focusing on predator activity — leopards, cheetahs, and crocodiles near the river banks.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Aegean Bliss Resort by late afternoon. Freshen up and enjoy a private sundowner on your villa's terrace. Dinner at the resort with a specially curated bush-to-coast themed menu.

meals.breakfast: Pre-dawn light breakfast at the resort before departure — Kenyan coffee, fresh pastries, and fruit
meals.lunch: Gourmet bush picnic in Tsavo East — artisan sandwiches, cold cuts, tropical fruit, and chilled sparkling water arranged by your guide
meals.dinner: Bush-to-coast dinner at the resort — wild game carpaccio, Tsavo-inspired slow-braised beef short rib, and passion fruit panna cotta

day_by_day.notes: Tsavo East is approximately 1.5–2 hours from the coastal resort area. Depart by 05:30 for the best wildlife viewing at sunrise. Wear neutral-colored clothing and bring binoculars. Rainfall in July is minimal (30mm/month) so game drives will be comfortable.

day_by_day.morning: Private helicopter transfer from the coast to Amboseli National Park (approx. 45 minutes scenic flight). Begin the Amboseli Elephant Watching with Kilimanjaro Views experience. Morning game drive through Amboseli's open savannah, observing some of Africa's largest elephant herds against the spectacular backdrop of snow-capped Mount Kilimanjaro.
day_by_day.afternoon: Guided walking safari near Amboseli's famous swamp areas with a Maasai guide — observe hippos, pelicans, and hundreds of bird species. Check into a luxury tented camp (pre-arranged day-use or overnight option) for an afternoon rest. Sundowner drive to Observation Hill for panoramic Kilimanjaro and elephant herd views.
day_by_day.evening: Traditional Maasai cultural evening at the camp — witness a boma visit, traditional jumping dances (Adumu), and stories around a campfire. Gourmet dinner under a canopy of stars in the African bush.

meals.breakfast: Full English and continental breakfast at Aegean Bliss before helicopter departure
meals.lunch: Gourmet bush lunch at the luxury tented camp — grilled meats, Kenyan salads, and chilled juices
meals.dinner: Candlelit bush dinner at the tented camp — three-course menu featuring Amboseli lamb, roasted root vegetables, and chocolate fondant with Kenyan vanilla cream

day_by_day.notes: Amboseli is best visited in the morning when Kilimanjaro is clearest before clouds build up. The helicopter transfer offers stunning aerial views of the Kenyan landscape. Confirm overnight vs. day-use arrangements at the tented camp in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning game drive in Amboseli — the best time to photograph elephants with Kilimanjaro at sunrise. Focus on bull elephant sightings and predator activity near the swamp edges. Guided bird-watching walk with a specialist ornithologist — Amboseli hosts over 400 bird species.
day_by_day.afternoon: Scenic helicopter or chartered flight transfer northward toward the Ol Pejeta Conservancy area. En route, enjoy aerial views of the Great Rift Valley. Arrive and check into a luxury conservancy lodge (pre-arranged). Afternoon visit to the Ol Pejeta Conservancy Chimpanzee Sanctuary — meet rescued chimpanzees from across Central and West Africa in a sensitively managed habitat.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive sundowner at a private lookout within Ol Pejeta Conservancy. Dinner at the lodge with a conservation-themed menu highlighting the conservancy's rhino and big cat protection programs.

meals.breakfast: Sunrise bush breakfast in Amboseli — freshly brewed Kenyan coffee, eggs cooked to order, and fresh fruit platters served in the open savannah
meals.lunch: In-flight or light arrival lunch at Ol Pejeta lodge — artisan wraps, local cheeses, and tropical juices
meals.dinner: Conservation dinner at Ol Pejeta lodge — three-course menu with locally sourced produce, featuring Kenyan highland lamb and a dessert of Kenyan honey cake

day_by_day.notes: The chimpanzee sanctuary visit requires a scheduled time slot — book in advance through the conservancy. Ol Pejeta is also home to the last two northern white rhinos in the world — a truly rare wildlife encounter.

day_by_day.morning: Exclusive early morning game drive within Ol Pejeta Conservancy — home to the Big Five plus chimpanzees and the world's last northern white rhinos. Focus on lion prides and leopard sightings in the acacia woodland. Visit the rhino sanctuary for an intimate guided rhino experience with the conservancy's dedicated rangers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Scenic drive or light aircraft transfer to Lake Nakuru National Park (approx. 1.5 hours). Check into a luxury lodge overlooking the lake. Begin the Lake Nakuru Flamingo and Rhino Safari — witness the alkaline lake shores painted pink by thousands of lesser and greater flamingos. Spot black and white rhinos, Rothschild's giraffes, and tree-climbing lions.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset boat ride on Lake Nakuru (if water levels permit) or lakeside sundowner with champagne. Dinner at the lodge featuring a lake-inspired menu.

meals.breakfast: Full lodge breakfast at Ol Pejeta before departure
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch en route to Lake Nakuru — gourmet sandwiches, fresh fruit, and sparkling water
meals.dinner: Lakeside dinner at Lake Nakuru lodge — smoked tilapia, Rift Valley vegetables, and passion fruit tart with Kenyan cream

day_by_day.notes: Lake Nakuru's flamingo numbers vary seasonally — July is generally excellent. The park is also a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Bring a telephoto lens for flamingo photography. The warm dry weather makes game viewing particularly rewarding.

day_by_day.morning: Dawn game drive in Lake Nakuru National Park — the early light is spectacular for photographing flamingos and the lake's diverse birdlife (over 450 species recorded). Visit the acacia forest zone for leopard and lion sightings. Stop at Baboon Cliff for panoramic views over the entire lake and its pink flamingo carpet.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private chartered flight to the Maasai Mara (approx. 45-minute scenic flight). Check into a luxury tented camp in the Mara. Begin the Maasai Mara Great Migration Safari — afternoon game drive to witness the world-famous Great Migration. In July, millions of wildebeest, zebras, and Thomson's gazelles are in the Mara ecosystem — prime river crossing season.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive private sundowner in the Mara bush with a butler and canapés. Return to camp for a lavish dinner under the African night sky with Maasai warriors as cultural hosts.

meals.breakfast: Early lodge breakfast at Lake Nakuru before the flight
meals.lunch: Welcome lunch at the Maasai Mara luxury tented camp upon arrival
meals.dinner: Gourmet bush dinner at the Mara camp — open-air dining with lanterns, featuring Mara-inspired cuisine: wild herb-crusted game, roasted plantains, and Kenyan chocolate mousse

day_by_day.notes: July is peak Great Migration season in the Mara — river crossings at the Mara River are the highlight. Your guide will position you at prime crossing points. Book the luxury Mara camp well in advance as July is the most sought-after month.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day Maasai Mara Great Migration Safari — depart at 06:00 for a full-day game drive. Station at the Mara River crossing points to witness the dramatic wildebeest river crossings with crocodiles lying in wait. Observe lion prides, cheetah coalitions, and elephant herds on the open plains.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the full-day game drive through the Mara Triangle — an exclusive conservancy zone with fewer vehicles and outstanding wildlife density. Bush lunch served in the field by your guide. Afternoon focus on predator activity — leopards in fig trees, hyena clans, and serval cats in the tall grass.
day_by_day.evening: Hot air balloon safari over the Maasai Mara at sunset (pre-book separately) — float silently over the migration herds and the golden savannah. Land for a private champagne toast on the plains. Return to camp for a special celebratory dinner.

meals.breakfast: Pre-dawn light breakfast at camp before the early game drive departure
meals.lunch: Full gourmet bush lunch in the Mara field — set up by camp staff with linen, silverware, and chilled wine
meals.dinner: Celebration dinner at the tented camp — five-course tasting menu with paired Kenyan wines and craft gins, featuring Mara lamb, truffle risotto, and a signature dessert platter

day_by_day.notes: The hot air balloon safari is one of Kenya's most iconic luxury experiences — book at least 3 months in advance for July dates. Balloon flights last approximately 1 hour and launch at dawn. Champagne breakfast on the plains is included with most operators.

day_by_day.morning: Final Maasai Mara game drive — a private morning drive with your dedicated guide focusing on any wildlife encounters you haven't yet experienced. Visit a local Maasai village (boma) for an authentic cultural immersion — learn about traditional beadwork, herding practices, and Maasai cosmology. Purchase handcrafted Maasai jewelry and artwork directly from artisans.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private chartered flight back to the Kenyan coast (approx. 1.5 hours scenic flight). Return to Aegean Bliss Resort. Afternoon at leisure — enjoy the resort's private beach, infinity pool, or indulge in a signature spa treatment. Optional: private yacht charter for a sunset coastal cruise along the Kenyan coastline.
day_by_day.evening: Private beach bonfire dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort — a bespoke dining experience on the sand with a personal chef, butler, and sommelier. Celebrate the safari journey with a curated menu and premium wine selection.

meals.breakfast: Full Mara camp breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Light in-flight snacks or welcome refreshments upon return to the resort
meals.dinner: Private beach bonfire dinner — grilled whole lobster, Swahili-spiced prawns, Kenyan coastal salads, and a decadent dessert of Mombasa coconut ice cream with caramelized pineapple

day_by_day.notes: The Maasai village visit should be arranged sensitively through your camp — ensure it is a community-endorsed experience that benefits the village directly. The private beach dinner requires advance arrangement with the resort's concierge team.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at leisure — enjoy a slow, indulgent breakfast on your private terrace. Last swim in the Indian Ocean or a final snorkeling excursion on the coral reef. Optional: deep-sea fishing charter for a few hours (arrange through the resort) or a private yoga session on the beach with a resort instructor.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spa and wellness afternoon — full body Swahili ritual treatment, hammam scrub, and aromatherapy massage at the resort's luxury spa. Pack and prepare for departure. Farewell meeting with your personal concierge — collect curated Kenyan gifts (single-origin coffee, Maasai crafts, and artisan chocolates) prepared by the resort.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at the resort's finest restaurant — a reflective, celebratory meal to close an extraordinary 10-day Kenyan journey. Private transfer to the airport for your onward flight.

meals.breakfast: Lavish farewell breakfast — full spread of Kenyan specialties including mandazi, fresh coconut, tropical fruits, eggs, smoked meats, and premium Kenyan single-origin coffee
meals.lunch: Light spa lunch — healthy grain bowls, fresh juices, and herbal teas at the resort's wellness café
meals.dinner: Farewell gala dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort's signature restaurant — seven-course chef's tasting menu celebrating the flavors of Kenya: coastal, savannah, and highland cuisines with premium wine pairing and a personalized dessert

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your departure flight time and arrange the airport transfer at least 24 hours in advance with the resort concierge. Allow 3 hours before international departure. Kenya has a 16% VAT on tourism services — confirm all bills are settled before checkout. Carry any wildlife souvenirs in checked luggage and ensure all purchases comply with CITES regulations.
